content.thinking:
I need to lay out the causal chain carefully, using placeholder names for every figure rather than writing numbers myself—covering the duration held, the error rate spike compared to baseline, and tracing why requests failed down to the underlying ValueError.

Tracing further, I'm distinguishing confirmed record evidence (deploy timing, rollback action) from the Investigator's candidate account about a stalled rollout—I need to flag that mixed-version replica state as an assumption, not confirmed fact, since only the rollback entry is directly verified. The root cause points to the deploy changing the shared cache entry format incompatibly, with old-revision replicas unable to parse the new composite format—leaving open why no compatibility test caught this before rollout.

For recovery, I'm noting the rollback action and associated entries. For contributing factors, I'm weighing the detection gap between onset and alert, the absence of a pre-deploy compatibility check, and whether the in-progress fix actually addresses read-compatibility across revisions. For action items, I'm drafting one around adding a cross-revision compatibility test or versioned cache keys, and another around detecting mixed-revision states or parse errors earlier.

I'm keeping the write-up free of specific timestamps, digits, or revision identifiers, using generic phrasing like "a composite entry" instead of exact log details.

action_items.item: Add a pre-deploy compatibility test that has the previous and the new revision each read cache entries written by the other. Adopt a two-step rule for shared-cache format changes: first ship a reader that accepts both formats, then switch the writer. Alternatively version the cache keys.
Add an alert on the summary-cache parse ValueError rate, and on a rollout that stays with more than one revision serving traffic for longer than expected, so a mixed-version break pages quickly.

causal_chain.step: Shoppers saw account page requests fail. The error rate went from {errors_before} to {errors_while_broken} on average over the broken period, peaking at {errors_at_worst}. The incident began at {began}.

The failing requests raised a ValueError because a summary cache entry in the composite amount/items form was not a figure in cents. This appeared in the logs from the onset and was highest at the worst minute.

Replicas running the old code parse a cache entry as a bare integer. They were reading entries in the new composite format. Only some summary reads failed, not all, which fits old and new revisions both being live and sharing one cache. The errors began right after the deploy at {P2.1}.

That deploy changed the cache entry format in the summary cache code, and the new format could not be read by the revision it replaced. The format change and the code that reads it shipped in a single step, so during the rollout each revision could write entries the other could not read.

Rolling back to the previous revision removed the mixed-version state. The service was back at its baseline from {recovered} and the paging rule stopped firing. This supports the format incompatibility between revisions as the cause.

contributing_factors.factor: Nothing checked, before or during the deploy, that the old and new revisions could read each other's entries in the shared cache. The format change was not staged to be backward compatible.

The page came after the onset, at {alert_raised} against an onset of {began}, so shoppers were affected for the span {alert_raised - began} before Argus was called in. Nothing flagged the cache parse errors or the mixed-revision rollout when they appeared.
The incompatible format change remains in the code base until the proposed fix is reviewed and merged. Redeploying it unchanged would repeat the failure.

input.executive_summary: For {duration}, a share of shoppers' account page requests failed. The error rate rose from {errors_before} to {errors_while_broken} on average and peaked at {errors_at_worst}. It began right after a new release was deployed. The release changed how a shared cache stores account summaries, and during the rollout the old and new versions could not read each other's entries. Argus rolled the service back to the previous revision. The error rate returned to its baseline and the alert stopped firing. Argus held the incident for {held}. A draft fix has been proposed and is awaiting review.

got_lucky: The failure was limited to the account page and ended as soon as the rollback removed the mixed-version state. Cache entries written in the new format did not cause lasting damage.
went_well: Argus read the metrics, logs and the recent deploy, and placed the onset at the deploy time.
The rollback was chosen quickly and its effect was confirmed against the metrics, which showed a return to baseline.
A draft fix was proposed as a pull request right after mitigation.
went_wrong: The incompatible cache format reached production with no compatibility check between consecutive revisions.
The alert fired after the onset, so shoppers saw failures before anyone was called in.

input.root_cause: The deploy at {P2.1} changed the shared summary-cache entry format from a bare cents figure to a composite amount-and-items string. It did not keep the format readable by the revision it replaced. While old and new revisions ran side by side against the same cache, old-revision replicas hit a ValueError reading entries written by new-revision replicas, and account page requests failed.
input.symptom: Account pages failed for some shoppers
